items.title: Egypt: Egypt, CIA Chief Affirm Support for Somalia's Sovereignty
items.description: [Radio Dalsan] Cairo -- Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi met with CIA Director John Ratcliffe in Cairo on Sunday, September 20, 2026, where both leaders reaffirmed support for Somalia's security and stability. The meeting, also attended by Egyptian General Intelligence Director Hassan Rashad, focused on regional developments including the situations in Somalia, Sudan, Gaza, and the Horn of Africa .

items.title: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany
items.description: According to a joint press release from the Darmstadt Public Prosecutor's Office and the South Hesse Police Headquarters, Mohamed Aweys Muudey, 68, an asylum seeker who had fled Somalia, was stabbed inside his communal accommodation by a 28-year-old suspect who is now in police custody. Muudey left Somalia in search of safety and protection. However, his life was cut short in a violent knife attack, highlighting the dangers many journalists in exile continue to face. He spent several years in prison in Ethiopia where he was arrested while seeking protection in 2014 before he was pardoned. Muud
items.titleIt: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany

items.title: SJS mourns Somali radio journalist Hassan Kafi Qoyste who died at 57
items.description: Ayanle Hassan, Qoyste's son, told SJS that his father, who was diabetic, fell ill on Friday night and was rushed to hospital, where he was pronounced dead. items.title: Somalia: NISA Arrests 11 Al-Shabaab Operatives in Security Operations Around Mogadishu
items.description: NISA said its forces arrested 11 operatives linked to the networks, which were allegedly being prepared to carry out activities threatening security. The networks were dismantled during planned security operations conducted in Darussalam, Garasbaley, Kahda, Daynile, and Afgoye. NISA forces also seized weapons and other materials that the operatives allegedly intended to use in their planned activities. The operations are part of NISA's ongoing efforts to prevent Al-Shabaab and other terrorist groups from carrying out activities aimed at undermining security and harming the Somali people.
items.titleIt: Somalia: NISA Arrests 11 Al-Shabaab Operatives in Security Operations Around Mogadishu

items.title: The Signature That Never Comes: Why Somalia's Clan Killers Walk Free
items.description: A death sentence in Somalia isn't final until the president signs it. Increasingly, none of them do.   That piece traced how Ahmed Shire Hussein, a Somali National Army soldier, was executed on camera near El Baraf for the crime of his father's clan — one entry in a pattern of hit squads, informant networks, and a tribal shield strong enough that a court willing to execute Al-Shabaab fighters would not touch a killer protected by his own sub-clan. Why does almost no one ever pay for it? This is the answer: what decides whether the state acts is the relative political power of the clans in
items.titleIt: The Signature That Never Comes: Why Somalia's Clan Killers Walk Free

items.title: Somalia: Blood, Blades, and Broken Streets: Inside the Terror Colonizing Mogadishu
items.description: Speaking after his son's funeral at Muuse Boqor Mosque the following day, veteran journalist Maxamed Cumar Baakaay put words to what the killing meant: "Allah gave me my son, and now Allah has taken him back. I praise Him. We have survived so many historic atrocities here in Mogadishu, only for me to lose my boy to the blades of the Ciyaal Weero." Family members say police have since detained several suspects, though authorities have not issued an official statement confirming the arrests. A journalist mourning his university-bound son has shattered the illusion of security in central Mogadish
items.titleIt: Somalia: Blood, Blades, and Broken Streets: Inside the Terror Colonizing Mogadishu

items.title: The Anatomy of a Blood Debt: How Clan Revenge Killings are Fracturing Somalia's Frontlines
items.description: Before he was executed, a chilling video captured his final moments. Stranded and defenseless, Hussein looked directly at his armed captors and uttered a devastating plea: "Abtiyaalow, ha i dilina" ("Maternal uncles, do not kill me"). The phrase was not just a desperate cry for mercy — according to clan elders and opposition figures interviewed for this piece, it reflected a specific and devastating reality. items.titleIt: The Anatomy of a Blood Debt: How Clan Revenge Killings are Fracturing Somalia's Frontlines

items.title: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany
items.description: According to a joint press release from the Darmstadt Public Prosecutor's Office and the South Hesse Police Headquarters, Mohamed Aweys Muudey, 68, an asylum seeker who had fled Somalia, was stabbed inside his communal accommodation by a 28-year-old suspect who is now in police custody. Muudey left Somalia in search of safety and protection. However, his life was cut short in a violent knife attack, highlighting the dangers many journalists in exile continue to face. He spent several years in prison in Ethiopia where he was arrested while seeking protection in 2014 before he was pardoned. Muud
items.titleIt: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany

items.title: Somali Journalist Mohamed Aweys Moodey Dies After Stabbing in Germany
items.description: The incident reportedly occurred at a residential facility. German authorities have identified a 28-year-old Somali man as the suspect. Police and prosecutors are investigating the circumstances of the incident, including the motive and whether it was connected to an earlier dispute between the two men. Moodey was a veteran journalist who worked in Somali media for many years. In 2014, he was arrested in Ethiopia and later sentenced to 27 years in prison under the country's anti-terrorism laws.
